messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty - PAGER fired for TempestCorp (dedicated-tenant t-tempest) - latency p95 > 2.5s and 503 rate 7% on cluster rwd-ded-42. Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/kb/dedicated-kv-fallback

pagerduty: Incident #PD-88431 triggered by alert rule tenant.high_p95_latency. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> oncall-sre.

alexa: acked. I'm on it, joining bridge.

sam: thx. looking at console metrics now, paging in prometheus: tenant_t_tempest_p95_latency spike starting ~1766659960. Also seeing kv_cache_evictions up 15x.

mohit: confirmed 503s correlated with KV miss ratio jump. Possibly kv TTL change from recent rollout? Tempest said they rolled model v3.2 two hours ago.

ryan: @alexa @mohit can you paste the pod logs for rwd-ded-42 pool? running `kubectl -n rwd-serving logs -l pool=rwd-ded-42 --tail 200` might show eviction churn.

alexa: pasted logs to thread:
```
E 11:22:31 kv_cache.cpp:274 eviction triggered, mem_usage 0.92, entries 4.2M
W 11:22:32 model_infer.cc:441 backend_error: backend returned 503 for request seq=...
I 11:22:35 routing: fallback to cheaper model variant tmp-v2
```

sam: noticed a bunch of short-lived keys. TTLs look like 30s. Tempest's new client-side caching maybe ignored?

mohit: temp hypothesis: model rollout changed prompt prefixes causing low cache reuse. Rapid cache churn -> KV eviction -> higher tail latency.

alexa: mitigation plan: 1) throttle Tempest requests to reduce write pressure 2) increase kv cache allocation on rwd-ded-42 3) roll Tempest back to v3.1 if needed. Anyone want to start throttle?

ryan: I can flip a soft throttle on their route. Command: `curl -X POST https://console.api.redwood/v1/tenants/t-tempest/controls/throttle -d '{"qps":50}'` (will rate-limit above 50 qps).

sam: I can bump kv cache size on pool rwd-ded-42 via infra API: `POST /infra/pools/rwd-ded-42/resize {"kv_cache_bytes": 2147483648}` - this will cause a rolling restart of pool agents (expect 45s disruption). Approve?

alexa: do it. we prefer minimal disruption -> do gradual step to 1.5GB first.

mohit: meanwhile I'll DM Tempest support to confirm the client-side TTL change. @support-bot can you open a customer-impact note?

support-bot: Created incident ticket CS-5598 for TempestCorp. Notifying account team.

pagerduty: PD note: incident assigned to alexa (oncall). Escalation in 8m if unacked.

sre-lead: quick Q: do we have canary/rollforward path that doesn't require full rollback? maybe change the route to a variant that preserves cache keys.

alexa: good idea. we have model aliasing. I'll pin their route to `redwood/model-tempest:v3.1-hotfix` for now. Command: `redwoodctl routes pin --tenant t-tempest --model v3.1-hotfix`

ryan: throttle applied (50 qps). Observability: ingress QPS dropped 62% for tenant, 503 rate trending down.

sam: started cache bump to 1.5GB now. infra reports rolling restarts, health-check passing.

mohit: temp support responded: they pushed a client change to reduce prefix normalization causing high cardinality keys. They've rolled that back to previous behavior and will push a fix in ~30m.

alexa: great. we should keep the temporary throttle + pin until kv evictions stabilize. Also let's add a temporary exception in routing to avoid fallback to tiny model variants that increase latency.

sre-lead: adding a short-term alert mute for alert rule tenant.high_p95_latency for t-tempest while we stabilize, to avoid noisy pages. Will expire in 1 hour.

pagerduty: PD update: ack by alexa. Escalation paused.

sam: metrics update 2m after action: p95 down from 2.8s -> 1.1s, 503s down from 7% -> 0.8%, kv_evictions down 70%. Looks good.

mohit: recommend follow-ups: 1) add per-tenant kv cache budgets + hard limits to prevent single tenant thrash 2) posterior: add pre-rollout smoke for TTL/key cardinality checks 3) Tempest to add client-side caching validation.

alexa: agreed. I'll open backlog tickets and assign to infra/product. Also customer comms: @support-bot please send Tempest an on-the-record update: what we did and next steps.

support-bot: Sent customer update to TempestCorp: initial mitigation performed (throttle + pin + infra bump). ETA for full resolution: 1-2 hours pending their fix.

ryan: rolling cache bump completed. No further restarts. KV eviction metric back to baseline.

alexa: removing route throttle now (incrementally). keeping model pin in place until Tempest confirms stable.

mohit: Tempest confirms internal tests stable, will run production traffic ramp slowly over 20m.

alexa: handing off to next oncall (ryan) for watch. I'll create incident summary and link runbook.

alexa: Incident summary (CS-5598 / PD-88431): cause: high kv-cache churn from client-side TTL/key changes after model rollout -> evictions -> increased tail latency & 503s. Mitigations: throttled tenant, increased kv cache allocation, pinned model to v3.1-hotfix, customer rollback. Impact: TempestCorp experienced elevated p95 and 503s for ~22m. Follow-ups: per-tenant kv budgets, rollout k/v cardinality smoke tests, update routing fallback policies.

ryan: ack, taking watch. thanks all. :thumbsup:

pagerduty: PD: status changed to acknowledged by alexa at 1766660068. PD timeline available: https://pagerduty.com/incident/PD-88431

incident-bot: Incident closed in Slack thread (auto-close after no regressions for 30m).
